etre-present.x: "être" means 'to be': "je suis", "tu es", "il est", "nous sommes", "vous êtes", "ils sont". Use it for identity, origin, profession and description. Learn it by heart, it is the most frequent verb in French. Examples: "je suis", "nous sommes", "ils sont".

avoir-present.x: "avoir" means 'to have': "j'ai", "tu as", "il a", "nous avons", "vous avez", "ils ont". It also forms the passé composé later. Note the elision "j'ai" before a vowel sound. Examples: "j'ai", "elle a", "nous avons".

il-y-a.t: Il y a: there is / there are
il-y-a.x: "il y a" introduces something that exists, singular or plural, and never changes: "il y a un livre", "il y a des livres". Negative: "il n'y a pas de livre". The question is "y a-t-il" or "est-ce qu'il y a". Examples: "il y a un café", "il n'y a pas de lait".

art-defini.x: "le" (masculine), "la" (feminine), "l'" (before a vowel) and "les" (plural) mean 'the'. French also uses them for general ideas: "j'aime la musique" means 'I like music'. Examples: "le café", "la pomme", "les enfants".

art-indefini.x: "un" (masculine), "une" (feminine) and "des" (plural) mean 'a', 'an' or 'some'. They introduce something new: "j'ai un frère et des cousins". "des" is often not translated in English. Examples: "un frère", "une sœur", "des amis".

gender-nouns.x: Every noun is masculine or feminine. Endings help: "-tion", "-té", "-ette" are mostly feminine, "-ment", "-age", "-eau" mostly masculine. Always learn a noun with its article: "la ville", "le village". Examples: "le village", "la ville", "la question".

plural-regular.x: Most plurals add "-s", which is silent: "un ami", "des amis". Nouns already ending in "-s", "-x" or "-z" do not change: "un pays", "des pays". Only the article and the liaison tell you it is plural. Examples: "deux sœurs", "trois amis".

plural-irregular.x: Nouns in "-al" change to "-aux": "un journal", "des journaux". Nouns in "-eau" and "-eu" add "-x": "un bateau", "des bateaux", "un jeu", "des jeux". Learn the few exceptions like "un festival, des festivals". Examples: "des journaux", "des bateaux", "des cheveux".

elision-basic.x: Short words "le", "la", "je", "ne", "de", "que", "se" lose their vowel before a vowel or mute h and take an apostrophe: "l'école", "j'aime", "n'aime pas", "qu'elle". "les" and "un" never elide. Examples: "l'école", "j'aime", "qu'elle".

contractions-au-du.x: "à + le" becomes "au", "à + les" becomes "aux", "de + le" becomes "du", "de + les" becomes "des". With "la" and "l'" nothing changes: "à la gare", "de la gare". Never write "à le" or "de le". Examples: "au marché", "aux voisins", "du professeur".

partitif.x: To talk about an amount of something you cannot count, use "du" (masculine), "de la" (feminine), "de l'" (vowel) or "des" (plural): "je prends du café". English often has no word here, French always does. Examples: "du pain", "de la salade", "des légumes".

de-negation.x: After "ne… pas", "jamais", "plus" an indefinite or partitive article becomes "de": "j'ai un chat" becomes "je n'ai pas de chat". Exception: after "être", keep the article: "ce n'est pas un chat". Examples: "pas de voiture", "jamais de viande".

adj-agreement.x: Adjectives agree with the noun: add "-e" for feminine and "-s" for plural. "grand", "grande", "grands", "grandes". Those ending in -e stay the same in the feminine: "un garçon sympa", "une fille sympa". Examples: "elle est grande", "ils sont petits".

adj-position.x: Most adjectives follow the noun: "une robe bleue". A few short, common ones go before: beauty, age, goodness, size ("beau, jeune, bon, grand, petit"): "un petit chien". "beau" has the forms "bel" and "belle". Examples: "une belle maison", "une maison blanche".

possessifs.x: The possessive agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: "mon père", "ma mère", "mes parents". Before a vowel, feminine nouns take "mon": "mon amie". Others: "notre/nos", "votre/vos", "leur/leurs". Examples: "mon père", "ma mère", "leurs chats".

demonstratifs.x: "ce" (masculine), "cet" (masculine before a vowel), "cette" (feminine) and "ces" (plural) mean 'this' or 'that'. Add "-ci" or "-là" to contrast: "ce livre-ci", "ce livre-là". Examples: "ce livre", "cette veste", "ces enfants".

pres-er.x: Remove "-er" and add "-e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent": "parler" gives "je parle", "tu parles", "il parle", "nous parlons", "vous parlez", "ils parlent". About 90 percent of French verbs follow this pattern. Examples: "je parle", "nous parlons", "ils parlent".

pres-ir-re.x: Regular "-ir" verbs add "-is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent": "finir", "je finis", "nous finissons". "-re" verbs add "-s, -s, -, -ons, -ez, -ent": "vendre", "je vends", "il vend". Examples: "je finis", "nous finissons", "je vends".

pres-irreguliers.x: Learn "aller" ("je vais, nous allons"), "faire" ("je fais, vous faites"), "prendre" ("je prends, ils prennent") and "venir" ("je viens, ils viennent"). Watch "vous faites" and "ils font", they break the pattern. Examples: "je vais", "nous faisons", "ils prennent", "vous venez".

tu-vous.x: Use "tu" with friends, family, children and peers. Use "vous" with strangers, older people, in shops and at work, and always when talking to several people. When in doubt, start with "vous". Examples: "tu viens", "vous venez".

on-nous.x: In everyday French "on" replaces "nous", but the verb stays in the third person singular: "on va au cinéma". "On" also means 'people in general': "en France, on mange du pain". Examples: "on va", "on mange".

neg-ne-pas.x: Put "ne" before the verb and "pas" after it: "je ne parle pas". Before a vowel "ne" becomes "n'": "il n'aime pas". In speech "ne" is often dropped, but write it in correct French. Examples: "je ne parle pas", "il n'aime pas".

q-est-ce-que.x: Easiest: keep the word order and raise your voice, or write a question mark: "tu viens ?". More formal: put "est-ce que" in front: "est-ce que tu viens ?". Before a vowel it becomes "est-ce qu'": "est-ce qu'elle vient ?". Examples: "tu aimes le thé ?", "est-ce que vous avez".

q-mots-interrogatifs.x: "où" (where), "quand" (when), "comment" (how), "combien" (how much), "pourquoi" (why), "qui" (who). They go at the start: "où est la gare ?". Answer "pourquoi" with "parce que". Examples: "où", "quand", "combien", "pourquoi".

q-quel.x: "quel" agrees with the noun: "quel" (m. sg.), "quelle" (f. sg.), "quels" (m. pl.), "quelles" (f. pl.). It can follow the noun after "être": "quel est ton nom ?" Examples: "quelle heure", "quels films".

futur-proche.x: Conjugate "aller" in the present and add an infinitive: "je vais travailler", "nous allons manger". Negative: "je ne vais pas partir". It is the usual way to talk about plans in speech. Examples: "je vais manger", "elle va partir".

pres-pronominaux.x: These verbs have a pronoun that matches the subject: "je me", "tu te", "il se", "nous nous", "vous vous", "ils se". Examples: "se lever", "se coucher", "s'habiller". Negative: "je ne me lève pas". Examples: "je me lève", "elle se couche".

imperatif-present.x: Use the present forms of "tu", "nous", "vous" without the pronoun: "tu parles" gives "parle !", "nous parlons" gives "parlons !", "vous parlez" gives "parlez !". "-er" verbs drop the final -s in the "tu" form. Irregular: "sois, soyons, soyez", "aie, ayons, ayez". Examples: "parle !", "parlons !", "parlez !".

modaux-pouvoir-vouloir.x: These three verbs are followed by an infinitive: "je veux manger", "tu peux venir", "nous devons partir". They are irregular: "je veux, nous voulons", "je peux, nous pouvons", "je dois, nous devons". Examples: "je veux partir", "tu peux", "nous devons".

prep-lieu.x: Common place words: "dans" (in), "sur" (on), "sous" (under), "devant" (in front of), "derrière" (behind), "entre" (between), "à côté de" (next to), "près de" (near). After "de", remember the contractions: "à côté du parc". Examples: "sur la table", "sous la table", "entre la poste et la banque".

prep-a-chez-de.x: "à" goes with towns and places: "je vais à Lyon". "chez" goes with people or their shop or home: "chez le dentiste", "chez moi". "de" says where you come from: "je viens de Lyon". Examples: "chez Marie", "à Lyon", "de la gare".

nombres.x: Special forms: "soixante-dix" (70), "quatre-vingts" (80, with an -s), "quatre-vingt-dix" (90). "et" appears in 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 and 71, but not in 81 and 91. Hyphens link tens and units. Examples: "vingt et un", "soixante-dix", "quatre-vingts".

heure-date.x: Use "il est" + hour: "il est trois heures et quart". "midi" and "minuit" take "et demi", other hours "et demie". Dates: "le 5 mai", only the 1st is ordinal: "le premier mai". Times use "à": "à neuf heures". Examples: "huit heures et demie", "le cinq mai".

c-est-ce-sont.x: Use "c'est" + singular noun and "ce sont" + plural noun to present or identify: "c'est un livre", "ce sont des livres". In speech "c'est" is also common with plurals. Question: "qu'est-ce que c'est ?" Examples: "c'est mon frère", "ce sont mes amis".

gouts-aimer.x: After "aimer", "adorer", "détester" and "préférer" use the definite article, not the partitive: "j'aime le café", "elle adore les chats". Add "beaucoup": "j'aime beaucoup la musique". Examples: "j'aime le chocolat", "je déteste les épinards".

adv-intensite.x: "très" goes before adjectives and adverbs: "très bien". "beaucoup" goes after verbs: "il travaille beaucoup". Before a noun use "beaucoup de": "beaucoup de fruits". "un peu" and "trop" work like "beaucoup". Examples: "très grand", "il mange beaucoup", "un peu".

avoir-expressions.x: French uses "avoir", not "être", for age and many body feelings: "j'ai vingt ans", "j'ai faim", "j'ai soif", "j'ai chaud", "j'ai froid", "j'ai peur", "j'ai sommeil". Add "très": "j'ai très faim". Examples: "j'ai faim", "elle a vingt ans", "il a froid".

clause-et-mais-parce-que.x: "et" adds, "ou" gives a choice, "mais" contrasts, "parce que" gives a reason. Before a vowel "parce que" becomes "parce qu'": "parce qu'il pleut". "donc" gives a result. Examples: "et", "mais", "parce que".

pc-avoir.x: Most verbs form the past with "avoir" in the present + past participle: "j'ai mangé", "tu as fini", "il a vendu". Participles: "-er" gives "-é", "-ir" gives "-i", "-re" gives "-u". Examples: "j'ai mangé", "nous avons fini".

pc-etre.x: About fifteen verbs use "être": "aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, rester, tomber, naître, mourir, retourner, passer" and all pronominal verbs. A memory aid is the list called "DR MRS VANDERTRAMP". Examples: "je suis allé", "elle est partie".

pc-accord-etre.x: With "être" the participle agrees with the subject: add "-e" for feminine and "-s" for plural. "il est parti", "elle est partie", "ils sont partis", "elles sont parties". Examples: "elle est partie", "ils sont venus", "elles sont allées".

pc-pronominaux.x: Pronominal verbs take "être", with the pronoun before it: "je me suis levé", "elle s'est couchée", "ils se sont promenés". The participle usually agrees with the subject. Examples: "je me suis levé", "elle s'est couchée".

pc-negation.x: Put "ne … pas" around the auxiliary, not the participle: "je n'ai pas mangé", "elle n'est pas venue". Same with "jamais", "plus", "rien": "il n'a rien dit". Examples: "je n'ai pas mangé", "il n'est jamais venu".

pc-participes-irreguliers.x: Must-know forms: "avoir" gives "eu", "être" gives "été", "faire" gives "fait", "prendre" gives "pris", "voir" gives "vu", "dire" gives "dit", "écrire" gives "écrit", "mettre" gives "mis", "pouvoir" gives "pu", "vouloir" gives "voulu". Examples: "j'ai eu", "j'ai été", "il a fait", "elle a pris".

imparfait-formation.x: Take the "nous" form of the present, remove "-ons", add "-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient": "nous parlons" gives "je parlais". Only "être" is irregular: "j'étais, nous étions". Examples: "je jouais", "nous allions", "il était".

imparfait-usage.x: Use the "imparfait" for the background of a story: weather, feelings, descriptions and repeated habits. "Il faisait beau", "j'étais fatigué", "chaque été, nous allions à la mer". Examples: "il faisait beau", "je jouais", "nous habitions".

impf-vs-pc.x: "Imparfait": what was going on, the setting. "Passé composé": what happened, one event that moves the story forward. "Je lisais quand le téléphone a sonné", the reading was ongoing, the ringing interrupted it. Examples: "je dormais", "le téléphone a sonné".

futur-simple.x: Take the infinitive (drop the final -e of "-re" verbs) and add "-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont": "parler" gives "je parlerai", "prendre" gives "je prendrai". Examples: "je parlerai", "nous prendrons", "ils finiront".

futur-irreguliers.x: The endings stay the same but the stem changes: "aller" gives "ir-", "être" gives "ser-", "avoir" gives "aur-", "faire" gives "fer-", "venir" gives "viendr-", "pouvoir" gives "pourr-", "voir" gives "verr-", "vouloir" gives "voudr-". Examples: "j'irai", "il fera", "ils viendront".

conditionnel-politesse.x: The "conditionnel" softens requests: "je voudrais" (I would like), "pourriez-vous" (could you), "j'aimerais" (I would love). Formation: futur stem + imperfect endings "-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient". Examples: "je voudrais", "pourriez-vous", "nous aimerions".

cod-pronoms.x: "le", "la", "l'" and "les" replace a noun without a preposition and stand before the verb: "je vois Paul" gives "je le vois". Negative: "je ne le vois pas". Examples: "je le vois", "elle la prend", "tu les aimes".

coi-pronoms.x: For people after "à", use "lui" (him or her) and "leur" (them): "je parle à Marie" gives "je lui parle", "je téléphone à mes parents" gives "je leur téléphone". "leur" never takes an -s here. Examples: "je lui parle", "elle leur écrit".

pronoms-me-te-nous-vous.x: These four pronouns work for both direct and indirect objects: "il me voit", "il me parle". Before a vowel "me" and "te" become "m'" and "t'": "je t'aime", "il m'écoute". Examples: "il me voit", "elle nous parle".

y-pronom.x: "y" replaces "à" + thing or a place: "je vais à Rome" gives "j'y vais". It stands before the verb: "nous y allons", "je n'y vais pas". Also "j'y pense". Examples: "j'y vais", "nous y allons".

en-pronom.x: "en" replaces "du, de la, des" + noun or "de" + noun. Keep the number: "j'ai deux frères" gives "j'en ai deux". Negative: "je n'en veux pas". Examples: "j'en veux", "nous en avons deux".

pronoms-toniques.x: Use "moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles" after prepositions ("avec moi", "chez eux"), for emphasis ("moi, je") and alone ("Qui est là ? Moi !"). Also after "c'est": "c'est lui". Examples: "avec moi", "chez lui", "eux".

comparatifs.x: Use "plus … que" (more), "moins … que" (less) and "aussi … que" (as … as) around an adjective or adverb: "elle est plus rapide que lui". For nouns use "plus de … que". Examples: "plus grand que", "moins cher que", "aussi rapide que".

superlatifs.x: Put the definite article before "plus" or "moins": "le plus grand", "la plus belle", "les moins chers". Say 'in' with "de": "le plus grand de la classe". Examples: "le plus grand", "la plus belle", "les moins chers".

meilleur-mieux.x: "bon" becomes "meilleur" (adjective, agrees): "une meilleure idée". "bien" becomes "mieux" (adverb, invariable): "elle chante mieux". Never say "plus bon" or "plus bien". Examples: "meilleur", "mieux", "la meilleure idée".

adverbes-ment.x: Add "-ment" to the feminine adjective: "lent" gives "lentement", "heureux" gives "heureusement". After a vowel, add it to the masculine: "vrai" gives "vraiment". "-ent" becomes "-emment": "prudent" gives "prudemment". Examples: "lentement", "vraiment", "prudemment".

prep-pays-villes.x: Cities: "à Paris", "de Paris". Feminine countries: "en France", "de France". Masculine countries: "au Japon", "du Japon". Plural countries: "aux États-Unis", "des États-Unis". Examples: "en France", "au Japon", "aux États-Unis", "à Paris".

depuis-pendant-il-y-a.x: "depuis" + present: something still going on ("j'habite ici depuis deux ans"). "pendant" + a duration: how long it lasted ("j'ai dormi pendant huit heures"). "il y a" + duration: how long ago ("il est parti il y a une heure"). Examples: "depuis deux ans", "pendant trois heures", "il y a une heure".

passe-recent.x: Conjugate "venir" in the present and add "de" + infinitive: "je viens de finir", "nous venons de partir". Before a vowel "de" becomes "d'": "il vient d'arriver". Examples: "je viens de manger", "ils viennent de partir".

imperatif-negatif.x: Wrap "ne … pas" around the imperative verb: "ne pars pas !", "ne partons pas !", "ne partez pas !". Pronouns stay before the verb: "ne le fais pas !". Examples: "ne parle pas", "ne partez pas".

imperatif-pronoms.x: In the affirmative imperative the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen: "regarde-moi", "parlez-nous", "dis-lui". "me" becomes "moi". Negative keeps the normal order: "ne me regarde pas". Examples: "regarde-moi", "dis-lui", "donne-le-moi".

rel-qui-que.x: "qui" replaces the subject: "la femme qui habite ici". "que" replaces the direct object: "le film que nous regardons". "que" becomes "qu'" before a vowel: "le livre qu'il lit". Examples: "l'homme qui parle", "le livre que je lis".

rel-ou.x: "où" links a place or a time to a clause: "la maison où elle habite", "le jour où nous sommes partis". It works for both place and time. Examples: "la ville où j'habite", "le jour où".

il-faut.x: "il faut" + infinitive means 'one must': "il faut partir". "il faut" + noun means 'you need': "il faut du temps". Negative "il ne faut pas" means 'you must not'. It is an impersonal verb: only "il". Examples: "il faut travailler", "il faut du temps".

neg-jamais-plus-rien.x: They replace "pas": "ne … jamais" (never), "ne … plus" (no more), "ne … rien" (nothing), "ne … personne" (nobody). "rien" and "personne" can also be the subject: "personne ne vient". Examples: "je ne mange jamais", "il ne travaille plus", "nous ne voyons personne".

quantite-de.x: After words of quantity use "de", no article: "beaucoup de travail", "un peu de sucre", "assez de temps", "trop de monde", "peu de gens", "une bouteille d'eau". Examples: "beaucoup de travail", "un peu de sucre", "trop de monde".

c-est-il-est.x: Use "il est" / "elle est" + adjective or profession alone: "il est médecin", "elle est gentille". Use "c'est" when there is an article or a possessive: "c'est un médecin", "c'est mon frère". Examples: "c'est un médecin", "il est médecin", "elle est gentille".

q-inversion.x: In careful French the verb moves before the subject pronoun, joined by a hyphen: "parlez-vous ?", "où vas-tu ?", "que font-ils ?". If the verb ends in a vowel, add "-t-": "aime-t-il ?". Examples: "parlez-vous", "où vas-tu", "que font-ils".

q-qui-que-quoi.x: "qui" asks about people, "que" and "qu'est-ce que" about things: "qu'est-ce que tu fais ?". After a preposition use "qui" (people) or "quoi" (things): "avec qui ?", "de quoi parles-tu ?". Examples: "qui est-ce ?", "qu'est-ce que tu fais ?", "de quoi parles-tu ?".

adj-irreguliers.x: These three have a special form before a masculine vowel: "beau" gives "bel", "nouveau" gives "nouvel", "vieux" gives "vieil". Feminine: "belle", "nouvelle", "vieille". Plural: "beaux", "nouveaux", "vieux". Examples: "un bel homme", "une nouvelle voiture", "un vieil ami".

connecteurs-temps.x: "d'abord" (first), "ensuite" or "puis" (then), "après" (after), "enfin" (finally) put actions in order: "d'abord je mange, puis je pars, enfin j'arrive". Examples: "d'abord", "ensuite", "puis", "enfin".

si-present-futur.x: For a real possibility: "si" + present in the condition, future (or imperative) in the result. "si tu viens, je serai content", "si vous avez le temps, appelez-moi". Never put the future after "si". Before "il" it is "s'il". Examples: "si tu viens, nous mangerons", "s'il pleut, je resterai".

savoir-connaitre.x: "savoir" is for facts and skills: "je sais nager", "je sais où il habite". "connaître" is for being familiar with people, places and things: "je connais Marie", "je connais cette ville". Examples: "je sais nager", "je connais Paris".

pres-irreguliers-2.x: Learn these in groups: "lire" ("nous lisons"), "dire" ("vous dites"), "écrire" ("ils écrivent"), "voir" ("nous voyons"), "boire" ("ils boivent"). The "nous" form helps to build the imparfait. Examples: "nous lisons", "vous dites", "ils écrivent".

meteo-il.x: Use "il fait" + adjective ("il fait beau, froid, chaud") and a verb for rain and snow ("il pleut", "il neige"). The subject "il" is empty and never changes. Question: "quel temps fait-il ?" Examples: "il fait beau", "il pleut", "il neige".

profession-sans-article.x: After "être", a profession, nationality or religion has no article: "il est médecin", "elle est française". With an adjective, add "c'est un" instead: "c'est un bon médecin". Examples: "elle est infirmière", "il est professeur".

subj-il-faut-que.x: After "il faut que" use the subjunctive. Regular verbs: take the "ils" present stem and add "-e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent": "ils partent" gives "que je parte". The "nous" and "vous" forms look like the imparfait. Examples: "il faut que tu viennes", "il faut que je parte".

subj-vouloir-que.x: When the subject changes, "vouloir que", "préférer que", "aimer mieux que" and "demander que" take the subjunctive: "je veux que tu viennes". If the subject is the same, use an infinitive: "je veux venir". Examples: "je veux que tu viennes", "elle veut que nous partions".

subj-irreguliers.x: Learn by heart: "être" ("que je sois"), "avoir" ("que j'aie, qu'il ait"), "aller" ("que j'aille"), "faire" ("que je fasse"), "pouvoir" ("que je puisse"), "savoir" ("que je sache"), "vouloir" ("que je veuille"). Examples: "que je sois", "qu'il ait", "que nous allions", "qu'ils fassent".

subj-emotions.x: After expressions of emotion ("être content que", "être triste que", "regretter que", "avoir peur que", "être surpris que") use the subjunctive when the subject changes. Examples: "je suis content que tu sois là", "elle regrette que nous partions".

subj-vs-indic.x: Certainty takes the indicative: "je pense que", "je sais que", "il est sûr que". Doubt, denial and will take the subjunctive: "je ne pense pas que", "je doute que", "il faut que". "Penser que" in a question can take either. Examples: "je pense qu'il a raison", "je ne pense pas qu'il ait raison".

subj-conjonctions.x: Some conjunctions always take the subjunctive: "pour que" (so that), "avant que" (before), "bien que" (although), "à condition que" (provided that), "jusqu'à ce que" (until). "après que" takes the indicative. Examples: "pour que tu comprennes", "avant que tu partes", "bien qu'il soit fatigué".

si-imparfait-cond.x: For imaginary or unlikely situations: "si" + imparfait, then conditional in the result. "si j'étais riche, je voyagerais". Never use the conditional after "si". Examples: "si j'avais de l'argent", "j'achèterais une maison".

cond-usage.x: The "conditionnel" gives advice ("tu devrais"), expresses wishes ("j'aimerais") and makes polite suggestions ("on pourrait"). With "devoir", "pouvoir" and "vouloir" it is very common. Examples: "tu devrais dormir", "nous aimerions voyager".

cond-passe-regret.x: For things that did not happen: "si" + plus-que-parfait, conditionnel passé. "si tu avais étudié, tu aurais réussi". The conditional passé is "avoir" or "être" in the conditional + past participle. Examples: "si j'avais su", "je serais venu".

plus-que-parfait-forme.x: Auxiliary in the "imparfait" + past participle: "j'avais mangé", "elle était partie", "nous nous étions levés". The same rules as the passé composé decide between "avoir" and "être" and for agreement. Examples: "j'avais fini", "nous étions partis", "elle avait mangé".

plus-que-parfait-usage.x: Use the "plus-que-parfait" for an action that happened before another past action or before a past moment: "quand je suis arrivé, il était déjà parti". It often explains a cause: "il était fatigué, il n'avait pas dormi". Examples: "le film avait déjà commencé", "il n'avait pas dormi".

di-present.x: With "dire que", "répondre que", "expliquer que" in the present, the tense of the reported clause does not change; only the pronouns and words like "mon" change: "« j'ai faim »" gives "il dit qu'il a faim". Examples: "il dit qu'il est fatigué", "elle répond qu'elle ne sait pas".

di-questions.x: Yes/no questions use "si": "il demande si tu viens". Question words stay: "où, quand, comment, pourquoi". "Qu'est-ce que" becomes "ce que", "qu'est-ce qui" becomes "ce qui". The word order is that of a statement. Examples: "il demande si je viens", "elle demande où j'habite".

di-passe.x: After "a dit que" the tenses shift back: present becomes "imparfait", futur becomes "conditionnel", passé composé becomes "plus-que-parfait". Time words change too: "demain" becomes "le lendemain". Examples: "il a dit qu'il était fatigué", "elle a répondu qu'elle viendrait".

gerondif-formation.x: Take the "nous" form of the present, remove "-ons", add "-ant", and put "en" before: "nous travaillons" gives "en travaillant". Exceptions: "être" gives "en étant", "avoir" gives "en ayant", "savoir" gives "en sachant". Examples: "en travaillant", "en lisant", "en finissant".

gerondif-usage.x: The "gérondif" says that two actions happen together ("il chante en travaillant"), how something is done ("on apprend en lisant") or a condition ("en tournant à gauche, vous verrez la poste"). Both verbs have the same subject. Examples: "on apprend en lisant", "il s'est blessé en jouant".

rel-dont.x: "dont" replaces "de" + noun: "je parle de ce livre" gives "le livre dont je parle". It also means 'whose': "la fille dont le père est médecin". Also after "avoir besoin de": "ce dont j'ai besoin". Examples: "le livre dont je parle", "la fille dont le père est médecin".

rel-ce-qui-ce-que.t: ce qui, ce que, ce dont
rel-ce-qui-ce-que.x: When there is no noun before, use "ce qui" (subject), "ce que" (object) and "ce dont" (with "de"): "ce qui se passe", "ce que tu veux", "ce dont j'ai besoin". Examples: "ce que tu veux", "ce qui se passe", "ce dont j'ai besoin".

pronoms-ordre.x: Order before the verb: "me, te, nous, vous" + "le, la, les" + "lui, leur" + "y" + "en". "me le", "te la", "nous les", but "le lui", "les leur": "je le lui donne". Examples: "je le lui donne", "elle me les envoie".

y-en-ensemble.x: When both "y" and "en" appear, "y" comes first: "il y en a", "il n'y en a plus". "en" keeps the quantity: "il y en a trois". Examples: "il y en a", "nous y en avons".

imperatif-ordre-pronoms.x: Affirmative: verb + direct object ("le, la, les") + indirect ("moi, lui, nous, leur") + "y" / "en": "donne-le-moi", "dis-le-lui". "moi" becomes "m'" before "en": "donne-m'en". Negative: normal order, "ne me le donne pas". Examples: "donne-le-moi", "dis-le-lui", "donne-m'en".

pronoms-possessifs.x: They replace a possessive + noun and agree with the noun: "le mien, la mienne, les miens, les miennes", "le tien", "le sien", "le nôtre", "le vôtre", "le leur". "Où est ma clé ? — Voici la mienne." Examples: "le mien", "la tienne", "les nôtres".

pronoms-demonstratifs.x: They replace 'the one(s)' and are followed by "de", "qui", "que", or "-ci / -là": "celui de gauche", "celle qui est ici", "ceux de Marc", "celles-là". Examples: "celui de gauche", "celle qui est ici", "ceux de Marc".

pronoms-indefinis.x: "quelqu'un" (someone), "quelque chose" (something), "personne" (nobody), "rien" (nothing), "chacun" (each one), "plusieurs" (several). Before an adjective use "de": "quelque chose de bon". Examples: "quelqu'un", "quelque chose de sucré", "chacun".

adj-indefinis.x: "chaque" + singular noun (each), "plusieurs" and "quelques" + plural noun (several, a few). "tout" agrees: "tout le monde", "toute la journée", "tous les jours", "toutes les semaines". Examples: "chaque élève", "plusieurs voitures", "toute la journée".

pc-accord-cod.x: With "avoir" the participle agrees with the direct object only when it comes before the verb: "j'ai acheté des fleurs" but "les fleurs que j'ai achetées", "je les ai vues". Examples: "les fleurs que j'ai achetées", "je les ai vues".

passif-forme.x: "être" (in the tense you need) + past participle that agrees with the subject + "par": "la lettre est écrite par Paul", "les maisons ont été détruites par le feu". The object of the active sentence becomes the subject. Examples: "le roman est écrit par", "la porte est ouverte par".

se-passif.x: A third-person verb with "se" gives a passive meaning, without an agent: "le vin se vend ici", "ça ne se dit pas", "cela se voit". Very common in speech and in rules. Examples: "ça se dit", "ce produit se vend partout".

etre-en-train-de.x: "être en train de" + infinitive stresses that an action is in progress right now: "je suis en train de lire". It is the equivalent of the English '-ing' when you want to insist: "ne l'appelle pas, il est en train de dormir". Examples: "je suis en train de manger", "ils sont en train de partir".

pc-avoir-transitif.x: When "sortir, monter, descendre, passer, rentrer, retourner" have a direct object, the auxiliary is "avoir": "j'ai sorti la voiture", "elle a monté les escaliers". Without an object, "être": "elle est sortie". Examples: "il a sorti la valise", "elle a monté les escaliers".

futur-anterieur.x: "avoir" or "être" in the futur simple + past participle: "j'aurai fini", "elle sera partie". It describes an action completed before another future action: "quand j'aurai fini, je t'appellerai". Examples: "quand j'aurai fini", "dès qu'elle sera arrivée".

quand-futur.x: Unlike English, French uses the future after "quand", "dès que", "lorsque" and "aussitôt que" when the action is in the future: "dès qu'il arrivera, nous partirons". "Si" is the exception: it never takes the future. Examples: "quand je serai grand", "dès qu'il arrivera".

connecteurs-cause-consequence.x: "car" and "parce que" give a reason; "comme" and "puisque" start the sentence with a known reason: "comme il pleut, je reste". "donc" and "alors" give the result: "il pleut, donc je reste". Examples: "donc", "car", "comme", "puisque".

connecteurs-opposition.x: "mais", "pourtant" and "cependant" oppose two ideas. "alors que" compares two facts: "elle aime le thé, alors que son mari préfère le café". "malgré" + noun means 'despite': "malgré la pluie". Examples: "pourtant", "alors que", "malgré la pluie".

but-pour-afin-de.x: With the same subject: "pour" or "afin de" + infinitive: "je travaille pour gagner de l'argent". With a different subject: "pour que" or "afin que" + subjunctive: "il parle lentement pour que nous comprenions". Examples: "pour gagner de l'argent", "afin de rentrer", "pour que nous comprenions".

neg-ne-que-ni.x: "ne … que" means 'only': "je n'ai que dix euros". "ne … ni … ni" means 'neither … nor': "elle ne mange ni viande ni poisson". "ne … aucun" means 'not any': "il n'a aucun ami". Examples: "je n'ai que dix euros", "ni viande ni poisson", "aucun ami".

neg-infinitif.x: Both parts of the negation go together before the infinitive: "ne pas partir", "ne plus fumer", "ne jamais mentir". "Il m'a demandé de ne pas fumer". Examples: "ne pas fumer", "ne plus travailler", "ne jamais mentir".

q-lequel.x: "lequel" replaces "quel" + noun and agrees: "lequel" (m. sg.), "laquelle" (f. sg.), "lesquels" (m. pl.), "lesquelles" (f. pl.). "Quel sac ? Lequel ?" After "à" and "de": "auquel", "duquel". Examples: "lequel", "laquelle", "lesquels".

exclamations.x: "quel" + noun: "quelle belle journée !". "comme" or "que" + clause: "comme il fait chaud !", "que c'est joli !". Note the space before "!" in French. Examples: "quelle belle journée !", "comme il fait chaud !", "que c'est joli !".

adv-place-pc.t: Short adverbs in the passé composé
adv-place-pc.x: Short common adverbs ("déjà, bien, mal, souvent, toujours, encore, trop, beaucoup") go between the auxiliary and the participle: "j'ai déjà mangé", "il a bien compris". Place adverbs and long adverbs go after. Examples: "elle a déjà fini", "il a bien compris".

comparatifs-avances.t: More and more, the more … the more
comparatifs-avances.x: "de plus en plus" (more and more), "de moins en moins" (less and less), "plus … plus" (the more … the more), "autant de … que" (as many as): "elle a autant de livres que moi". Examples: "de plus en plus froid", "plus on travaille, plus on apprend", "autant de livres".

prep-verbes.x: Many verbs need a fixed preposition: "penser à", "s'intéresser à", "répondre à", "parler de", "avoir besoin de", "avoir envie de", "rêver de". Learn them with the verb. Examples: "penser à", "parler de", "avoir besoin de", "s'intéresser à".

prep-temps-en-dans.x: "dans" + duration: when something will happen, counted from now ("le film commence dans une heure"). "en" + duration: how long something takes ("il a lu ce livre en deux jours"). "en" also goes with months and years: "en mai", "en 1998". Examples: "dans une heure", "en deux jours".

inf-apres-prepositions.x: "avant de" + infinitive, "après" + past infinitive ("avoir" or "être" + participle), "sans" + infinitive: "avant de partir", "après avoir mangé", "sans dire au revoir". The subject must be the same. Examples: "avant de manger", "après avoir mangé", "sans dire".

faire-causatif.x: "faire" + infinitive means to have something done ("je fais réparer ma voiture") or to make someone do something ("il fait rire les enfants"). The infinitive follows "faire" directly. Examples: "je fais réparer ma voiture", "il fait rire les enfants".

verbes-perception.x: After "voir", "entendre", "regarder", "écouter", "sentir" put an infinitive: "je les entends jouer", "nous voyons passer le train". The pronoun is the object of the perception verb. Examples: "je les entends chanter", "nous voyons passer le train".

voyelle-liaison-ecrite.x: Before a vowel or mute h some words change to ease pronunciation: "ma" becomes "mon" ("mon amie"), "ce" becomes "cet" ("cet homme"), "beau" becomes "bel" ("un bel arbre"), "nouveau" becomes "nouvel", "vieux" becomes "vieil". Examples: "mon amie", "cet homme", "un bel arbre".

tout-tous-toutes.x: As an adjective "tout" agrees: "tout le monde", "toute la journée", "tous les jours", "toutes les semaines". As a pronoun it means 'everything' ("j'ai tout compris") or 'all' ("ils sont tous là", with the final -s said). Examples: "tous les jours", "toute la journée", "ils sont tous là".

subj-after-bien-que.x: "bien que", "quoique" and "encore que" express concession and always take the subjunctive, even when the fact is certain. Say "Bien que le projet soit coûteux, nous continuons", not "bien que le projet est". Examples: "Bien qu'il pleuve, nous sortons", "Quoiqu'elle soit jeune, elle dirige l'équipe".

subj-after-pour-que.x: "pour que" and "afin que" introduce a purpose and are followed by the subjunctive. The subject of the purpose clause is usually different from the main subject: "Je répète pour que vous compreniez". With the same subject, use "pour" or "afin de" plus an infinitive. Examples: "Il parle lentement pour que nous comprenions", "Elle écrit afin que tout soit clair".

subj-after-avant-que.x: "avant que" and "jusqu'à ce que" take the subjunctive because the action is not yet realised. After "avant que" a "ne" is often added, with no negative meaning: "avant qu'il ne parte". Use "avant de" plus infinitive if the subject is the same. Examples: "Attends jusqu'à ce que je revienne", "Appelle avant que nous ne partions".

subj-a-moins-que-ne.x: "à moins que" means "unless" and requires the subjunctive. Formal French often adds an expletive "ne" before the verb ("à moins qu'il ne vienne"), which is not a real negation. Do not use the conditional or the future after it. Examples: "Je sors, à moins qu'il ne pleuve", "à moins que vous ne soyez occupé".

subj-a-condition-que.x: "à condition que" and "pourvu que" mean "provided that" and take the subjunctive, never the future or conditional. "Pourvu que" can also open a sentence to express a hope: "Pourvu qu'il vienne !". Examples: "Je viendrai à condition que vous m'invitiez", "Pourvu que tout se passe bien".

subj-vs-ind-opinion.x: After "penser que" and "croire que" in the affirmative, use the indicative: "Je pense qu'il a raison". In the negative or in an inverted question, doubt appears and the subjunctive is used: "Je ne pense pas qu'il ait raison". The mood follows how certain the speaker is. Examples: "Je crois qu'elle viendra", "Je ne crois pas qu'elle vienne".

subj-emotion-doubt.x: Verbs of emotion ("être content que", "regretter que"), doubt ("douter que") and necessity ("il faut que", "il est essentiel que") are followed by the subjunctive when the subjects differ. The clause expresses a reaction or a need, not a plain fact. Examples: "Je suis ravi que vous veniez", "Il faut que nous partions".

subj-irregular-forms.x: Seven common verbs have irregular subjunctive stems: "être" (sois, soyons), "avoir" (aie, ayons), "aller" (aille, allions), "faire" (fasse), "pouvoir" (puisse), "savoir" (sache), "vouloir" (veuille). Learn them as whole forms; the nous and vous forms of "être", "avoir", "aller" and "vouloir" also have their own stems. Examples: "qu'elle aille", "que vous sachiez", "que tu aies".

subj-passe.x: The past subjunctive is the subjunctive of "avoir" or "être" plus the past participle. It shows that the action is finished before the action of the main verb: "Je suis content que tu sois venu". Choose the auxiliary as in the passé composé and keep the agreement. Examples: "Il faut qu'ils aient fini", "Bien qu'elle soit partie".

subj-vs-infinitive.x: When the subject of both verbs is the same, French prefers the infinitive: "Je veux partir". When the subject changes, use "que" plus the subjunctive: "Je veux que tu partes". The same applies to wishes, emotions and many conjunctions ("avant de" or "avant que"). Examples: "Elle est contente d'être là", "Elle est contente que vous soyez là".

subj-superlative-relative.x: After a superlative ("le plus", "le meilleur") or "seul", "premier", "dernier", "unique", the relative clause takes the subjunctive, because the statement expresses a personal judgement. With "jamais" the past subjunctive is common: "le plus beau film que j'aie vu". Examples: "le seul homme qui sache", "la première fois que je le voie".

subj-relative-search.x: When a relative clause describes something you are looking for, wish for, or doubt exists, use the subjunctive: "Je cherche un livre qui soit simple". If you know the thing exists, use the indicative: "J'ai un livre qui est simple". Typical triggers: "chercher", "vouloir", "il n'y a personne qui", questions about existence. Examples: "Y a-t-il quelqu'un qui puisse m'aider ?".

cond-passe-news.x: Journalists use the conditional, often the past conditional, to report information that is not confirmed: "Le ministre aurait démissionné". It signals "reportedly" or "allegedly" and keeps the writer from vouching for the fact. Use the conditional present for a current rumour: "Il serait malade". Examples: "Deux personnes seraient blessées", "selon certaines sources, le vol aurait été annulé".

si-plus-que-parfait.x: For an unreal condition in the past, use "si" plus the plus-que-parfait, and the past conditional in the result: "Si j'avais su, je serais venu". Never put a conditional after "si" in this meaning. The result clause shows what did not happen. Examples: "Si elle avait étudié, elle aurait réussi", "Si nous étions partis, nous aurions vu le concert".

si-mixed-conditions.x: A mixed conditional links a past condition with a present result: "si" plus plus-que-parfait, then the present conditional. Time words such as "maintenant" or "aujourd'hui" in the result show that the consequence is still true now. Example: "Si tu avais écouté, tu comprendrais". Compare with the fully past pattern: "tu aurais compris".

hypothese-au-cas-ou.x: "au cas où" expresses a precaution against a possible event and is followed by the conditional, not the subjunctive or the future. It means "in case" or "just in case". It can stand at the start or the end of the sentence. Examples: "Prenez un parapluie au cas où il pleuvrait", "Au cas où tu serais en retard, appelle-moi".

apres-que-indicatif.x: "après que" and "dès que" state a fact that really happened, so they take the indicative, not the subjunctive (unlike "avant que"). The verb after "après que" is in a compound tense, earlier than the main verb: "Après qu'il a fini, il est rentré". After "dès que" with a future main verb, use the futur antérieur: "Dès que tu auras fini, appelle-moi".

concordance-des-temps.x: When the main verb is in the past, the verb in the subordinate clause moves back: present becomes imparfait, passé composé becomes plus-que-parfait, future becomes conditional. Do not mix a past main verb with a present subordinate verb: "Il pensait que nous étions partis". Examples: "Je savais que tu viendrais", "Elle disait qu'elle était fatiguée".

discours-indirect-passe.x: In reported speech after a past verb ("elle a dit que"), shift the tenses: present to imparfait, passé composé to plus-que-parfait, future to conditional. Time words change too: "demain" becomes "le lendemain", "hier" becomes "la veille", "aujourd'hui" becomes "ce jour-là". Example: "Il a dit qu'il viendrait le lendemain".

discours-indirect-questions.x: In indirect questions, use normal word order with no question mark. "Est-ce que" and yes/no questions become "si": "Il a demandé si je venais". "Qu'est-ce que" becomes "ce que", and "qu'est-ce qui" becomes "ce qui". Tenses shift after a past verb. Examples: "Elle m'a demandé ce que je voulais", "Il voulait savoir ce qui se passait".

discours-indirect-ordres.x: To report a command or request, use "dire de" or "demander de" plus an infinitive: "Elle m'a dit de rentrer". The person addressed takes "à" or a pronoun: "Il a demandé à ses voisins de baisser la musique". A negative order keeps "ne pas" together before the infinitive: "Il nous a dit de ne pas toucher aux câbles".

accord-participe-cod-avant.x: With "avoir", the past participle agrees with the direct object only when it comes before the verb. Look for "que", a pronoun like "les" or a question word: "Les lettres que Marie a écrites", "Quelle robe as-tu choisie ?". If the object follows, there is no agreement: "Marie a écrit des lettres".

accord-participe-pronominaux.x: In the passé composé of a pronominal verb, the participle agrees with the reflexive pronoun when it is a direct object: "Les amies se sont retrouvées". It stays invariable when the pronoun is indirect or another object follows: "Elle s'est lavé les mains", "Ils se sont envoyé des messages". Ask yourself whether "se" means "à qui ?" or "qui ?".

participe-present-gerondif.x: The gerund "en + -ant" says how or when something happens and is invariable: "Il s'est blessé en coupant du bois". The present participle replaces a clause and is also invariable: "Les enfants jouant dans le jardin". The verbal adjective agrees with its noun: "une histoire fascinante", "des résultats surprenants".

passif-et-alternatives.x: The passive uses "être" + participle: "Les résultats ont été annoncés par le jury". French often prefers alternatives: a reflexive for general facts ("Le fromage se mange après le plat"), "on", or "se faire" for something that happens to the subject ("Il s'est fait voler son sac").

causatif-faire-laisser.x: "Faire" + infinitive means to cause something to be done: "Nous avons fait refaire la cuisine". "Laisser" + infinitive means to allow: "Le professeur a laissé les élèves partir". The participle "fait" stays invariable before the infinitive: "Ce film m'a fait pleurer".

pronoms-relatifs-composes.x: After a preposition, use "lequel", "laquelle", "lesquels" or "lesquelles", matching the noun: "la table sur laquelle", "les amis chez lesquels". With "à" they contract: "auquel", "auxquels", "auxquelles", "à laquelle". With "de" they give "duquel", "desquels", "de laquelle".

pronom-relatif-dont.x: "Dont" replaces "de" + noun in a relative clause: "L'ordinateur dont j'ai besoin" (avoir besoin de). It also expresses possession, with the noun directly after it: "l'écrivain dont le dernier roman". And it introduces a part of a group: "trois enfants, dont deux vivent à l'étranger".

ce-qui-ce-que-ce-dont.t: Ce qui, ce que, ce dont
ce-qui-ce-que-ce-dont.x: "Ce" + relative pronoun refers to an idea or unnamed thing. "Ce qui" is the subject ("Ce qui m'inquiète"), "ce que" the object ("ce que tu veux"). Use "ce dont" for verbs with "de" ("ce dont tu as envie") and "ce à quoi" for verbs with "à" ("ce à quoi il s'intéresse").

pronoms-doubles-ordre.x: Before the verb, put the indirect pronoun first for me, te, nous and vous: "Je te le rends". For third persons, the direct pronoun comes first: "Je le lui donne"; "en" always comes last: "Je lui en ai parlé". After an affirmative imperative, the order is direct then indirect: "Donne-les-moi".

pronoms-y-en-avances.x: "En" replaces "de" + noun or a quantity, and the number stays: "J'en ai acheté trois". "Y" replaces "à" or a place: "J'y pense tout le temps". In the affirmative imperative they follow the verb and combine: "Donnez-m'en un kilo".

mise-en-relief.x: "C'est ... qui" highlights the subject and "c'est ... que" highlights an object or a complement: "C'est moi qui ai fait le gâteau", "C'est demain que nous partons". With a plural noun, use "ce sont": "Ce sont mes voisins que j'ai invités". The verb after "qui" agrees with the stressed element.

inversion-peut-etre.x: In formal French, "peut-être", "sans doute" and "aussi" (meaning therefore) at the start take subject-verb inversion: "Peut-être viendra-t-il demain". With a noun subject, repeat it as a pronoun. Add "-t-" when the verb ends in a vowel before "il" or "elle": "viendra-t-elle".

ne-expletif.x: After verbs of fear ("craindre que"), "avant que" and comparatives of inequality, formal French adds a "ne" that carries no negative meaning: "Je crains qu'il ne pleuve", "avant qu'il ne fasse nuit", "plus grand que je ne pensais". It is optional in speech, never takes "pas".

connecteurs-concession-opposition.x: "Bien que" + subjunctive and "malgré" + noun express concession: "Malgré la pluie, nous sommes sortis". "Alors que" + indicative contrasts two facts: "Paul adore la mer, alors que sa femme préfère la montagne". "Pourtant", "cependant" and "en revanche" link two sentences.

nominalisation.x: Nominalisation makes writing more concise and formal. Verbs become nouns with endings like -tion, -ment, -ure or -ée: "ouvrir" gives "l'ouverture", "augmenter" gives "l'augmentation", "arriver" gives "l'arrivée". Adjectives work too: "difficile" gives "la difficulté". Check the gender of the new noun.

tout-accord.x: As an adjective, "tout" agrees with the noun: "tous les magasins", "toutes les fenêtres". As an adverb meaning "quite", it is invariable, except before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant: "elle est tout étonnée" but "elles sont toutes timides".

prepositions-apres-verbes.x: Some verbs take a fixed preposition, and it can change the meaning. "Penser à" means to think about: "Je pense à mes vacances"; "penser de" asks for an opinion: "Que penses-tu de ce film ?". Learn pairs like "s'habituer à" and "se méfier de" as a unit.

infinitif-passe.x: "Après" + "avoir" or "être" + past participle says an action happened before the main one: "Après avoir écrit la lettre, il l'a postée". Both actions must have the same subject. Verbs of movement and pronominal verbs use "être" and agree: "Après être rentrée", "Après nous être reposés".

a-regard-pronoms-lequel.x: "Lequel" asks for a choice among known items and agrees with them: "Lequel de ces chemins ?", "Laquelle de tes amies ?". With "à" or "de" it contracts: "Auquel de ces clients as-tu téléphoné ?", "Duquel parles-tu ?". Use "quel" only directly before a noun.
